cards.title: Introduction to Java Data Types
cards.content:
Java is a strongly-typed language, which means every variable must be declared with a specific data type before it can be used.

Java data types are divided into two main categories:

  • Primitive Data Types: Predefined by the language (e.g., int, char, boolean).
  • Reference/Object Data Types: Created by the programmer or provided by classes (e.g., String, Arrays, Classes).

cards.title: The 8 Primitive Data Types
cards.content:
Java has exactly 8 primitive data types, designed for maximum efficiency in memory and performance:

TypeSizeDefault Value
byte1 byte (8-bit)0
short2 bytes (16-bit)0
int4 bytes (32-bit)0
long8 bytes (64-bit)0L
float4 bytes (32-bit)0.0f
double8 bytes (64-bit)0.0d
char2 bytes (16-bit Unicode)'\u0000'
boolean1 bit (virtual)false

cards.title: Understanding Reference Types
cards.content:
Unlike primitive types, Reference Types point to objects stored in the memory heap.

  • They default to null if not explicitly initialized.
  • They can be used to call methods (e.g., string.toUpperCase()).
  • Common reference types include class objects, interface types, and arrays.
String message = "Hello Java!"; // Reference type
int number = 10;                // Primitive type

cards.title: Type Casting in Java
cards.content:
Type casting is assigning a value of one primitive data type to another type.

There are two types of casting in Java:

  1. Widening Casting (automatically): Converting a smaller type to a larger type size. 
    int myInt = 9;
double myDouble = myInt; // Automatic casting: int to double
  2. Narrowing Casting (manually): Converting a larger type to a smaller type size. 
    double myDouble = 9.78d;
int myInt = (int) myDouble; // Manual casting: double to int

cards.title: Key Takeaways
cards.content:
Congratulations! You have completed the Java Data Types module.

Remember:

  • Primitives are high-performance and live on the Stack.
  • References refer to instances of classes and live on the Heap.
  • Always watch for precision loss when applying manual casting!
